answer: Using a logistic regression of remission on age, BMI, and gender (n = 80; remission coded as Efficacy = PR vs SD/PD), the change in log-odds of remission for each one-year increase in patient age is **−0.0795** (SE = 0.0263; 95% CI −0.1311 to −0.0280; p = 0.0025). Equivalently, each additional year of age is associated with an odds ratio for remission of **0.924** (95% CI 0.877–0.972), i.e., roughly a 7.6% decrease in the odds of remission per year of age, holding BMI and gender constant. The PR = remission mapping is inferred from the data (no explicit remission column exists; Efficacy = PR in all 41 Group-1 patients and SD/PD in all 39 Group-2 patients); Age, BMI, and Gender are continuous/continuous/dummy (Female = 1, Male reference) predictors; the model converged normally (pseudo-R² = 0.124, overall LR p = 0.0033), and a sensitivity check with the alternative outcome mapping (remission = non-PD) yields a similar age coefficient of −0.0605 (SE 0.0283).
